o: Describe how an operating system provides a user interface.
Explain allocation of memory and how an OS supports multitasking.
Choose suitable interfaces for different users.
c: System software coordinates hardware and applications, and provides services such as a user interface, memory management and security. Without it, applications would have to manage many hardware details.
A GUI lets users select icons, windows and menus, making common tasks approachable. A CLI accepts typed commands, which can be efficient for an experienced user and automation.
The OS allocates available RAM to applications, manages which data is kept in RAM and moves data as needed. Paging and segmentation are not required for this specification.

The OS manages running applications and shares processor time; it allocates memory and handles resources so users can switch between tasks. Switching does not mean one CPU core necessarily runs every task at exactly the same instant.

m.title: OS manages several applications
m.q: A student has a browser, music app and editor open. Explain how the OS manages their memory and allows multitasking. [4 marks]
st: Identify the three applications competing for resources.
The OS allocates space in RAM to applications [1], keeping their required data available [1].
The OS manages CPU time among tasks [1], so the student can switch between or use different applications [1].
Four linked marks: memory allocation, purpose, processor time, multitasking.

w: A receptionist runs booking software and an email client together. Explain TWO ways the OS helps these applications operate. [4 marks]

The OS allocates available RAM to each application [1], allowing program data to be held in primary memory [1]. It manages CPU time or resources [1], letting both applications remain usable through multitasking [1].
A technician prefers typed commands for repetitive setup tasks. Explain one benefit and one drawback of a CLI compared with a GUI. [4 marks]
A CLI can run repeated or scripted commands efficiently [1], speeding up frequent technical tasks [1]. Users must remember accurate commands [1], so beginners may find it harder and make errors [1].
A computer has three programs open but limited RAM. Explain TWO memory-management problems the OS must handle. [4 marks]

The OS must allocate the available RAM across programs [1] to prevent applications from competing for the same allocated space [1]. It manages moving/loading application data in memory [1], so programs have needed data as the user switches between them [1].

k.q: Simulate checking whether there is enough RAM to open a photo editor using values in megabytes (MB).
k.code:
freeMb = 1200
editorMb = 850
if freeMb >= editorMb then
    print("Editor can be loaded")
else
    print("Not enough free RAM")
endif
p: Predict the output when freeMb is 1200.
Change freeMb to 700 and predict the output.
Add a variable browserMb = 250 and calculate how much RAM would remain after opening both programs (if enough).
k.a:
Original: Editor can be loaded. With freeMb = 700: Not enough free RAM.

Possible extension:
freeMb = 1200
editorMb = 850
browserMb = 250
neededMb = editorMb + browserMb
print(freeMb - neededMb)

Output: 100 MB free in this simplified model.

e:
State TWO functions of an operating system. [2 marks]

Source: Original OCR J277-style teaching question; not an official past-paper question.
Provides a user interface [1]; allocates/manages RAM for applications [1]. Other valid functions include file, device, user management and multitasking.

A photographer switches between photo-editing software and a browser. Explain how operating-system memory management and multitasking support this. [4 marks]

Source: Original OCR J277-style teaching question; not an official past-paper question.
OS allocates RAM to each program [1] so needed data is available [1]. It manages the running tasks and processor time [1], so the user can switch between programs while both remain active [1].

Compare GUI and CLI interfaces for an office worker and explain the OS role in memory management. [6 marks]

Source: Original OCR J277-style teaching question; not an official past-paper question.

GUI uses visual windows/icons and menus [1], making routine functions easier to discover [1]. CLI takes typed commands [1] that can be efficient for expert repetitive tasks [1]. OS allocates RAM to programs [1], allowing applications to run with required data in memory [1].
v: System software managing hardware/resources and supplying services to programs.
Graphical User Interface using windows, icons, menus and a pointer.
Command Line Interface using text commands.
Allocation and management of RAM for running programs.
Coordinating the execution of multiple applications.
Means by which the user interacts with a computer.
Volatile primary memory holding active programs and data.
x: The operating system can allocate RAM to different applications to help them run.
r: In Lesson 036, an unclear answer said that a firewall 'makes the Internet safe'. Explain precisely how a firewall filters traffic. [2 marks]
A firewall uses configured rules to check network traffic [1] and blocks disallowed traffic/connections [1].
Assessment Q1. State what LAN and WAN mean, and identify the device that forwards data between networks. [3 marks]
Local Area Network [1]; Wide Area Network [1]; router [1].
State one job of the ALU and one job of the Control Unit. [2 marks]
ALU performs arithmetic/logic [1]. CU coordinates CPU activities and instruction decoding [1].
Assessment Q2. A public library uses a school-style star LAN to share files and printers. Explain one advantage of the topology and one potential weakness. [4 marks]

Central switch simplifies adding/managing devices [1], allowing easier administration [1]. The central switch is a single point of failure [1], so if it fails connected devices may be unable to communicate [1].
